A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Zebra-CoT and retain the same dataset and core training experiments. The text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Anole fine-tuning results in Table 2 and Appendix C, together with generated Bagel reasoning examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds frontier-model scaffolding experiments in Section 4 and Table 8, plus Bagel performance findings in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The data-curation pipeline, Anole fine-tuning procedure, and Bagel adaptation are retained, including the vision-start loss and inference-time switching between text and image generation. Scaffolding is introduced as an evaluation experiment rather than a revision of these methods.

E1.justification: The 182,384-example corpus, its task categories, and the seven external benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 adds assisted evaluation scenarios in which models receive one or two known multimodal reasoning steps, using six existing task families rather than new domains.

E2.justification: Table 8 introduces question-only versus scaffolded comparisons for GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Appendix D also adds comparison with the original Bagel model generating text-only responses. The existing base-Anole comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new scaffolding study selects 512 questions across six task families, compares question-only, one-step, and two-step conditions, and uses GPT-4.1 to judge accuracy. This adds a substantial evaluation protocol; the original Anole and Bagel training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a cross-model study of sensitivity to the number of supplied reasoning steps, with task-level results in Table 8. Appendix B adds five Bagel output examples, and Appendix D adds qualitative failure analysis of hallucinated images and their effects on subsequent reasoning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new scaffolding results report point accuracies and averages across models, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports average frontier-model accuracy of 31.51% with questions alone, 47.99% with one supplied step, and 56.70% with two steps, alongside detailed Table 8 results. It also reports no substantial Bagel improvement and slight declines on tasks such as MathVista. These are new findings; the retained numerical values in Tables 2–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: No theoretical result, proof, or formal derivation concerning the proposed work is added or revised. The new scaffolding notation describes experimental inputs, while the additional mathematical examples are generated model outputs.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a main contribution claiming that Zebra-CoT challenges frontier models and that supplied multimodal traces substantially improve their performance. This expands the paper's central claims beyond dataset construction and fine-tuning, while retaining the original dataset and model claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 interprets scaffolding gains as evidence of trace quality and visual-CoT utility, and argues that partial traces guide reasoning without revealing answers. Appendix D adds an important limitation: Bagel's generated-image hallucinations can propagate through its understanding encoder and reduce accuracy, qualifying the earlier emphasis on successful visual generation.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses use of mini versions of MathVision and MathVista, explains Bagel's two visual encoders, and adds Bagel component and licensing information. It removes the explicit Anole test counts of 6/142 and 24/142 while retaining their percentages. Core hyperparameters and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GPT-5, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, Yang et al. (2024) on video-based decision making, and Zhu et al. (2020), BabyWalk. The principal related-work framework and positioning against existing visual-CoT and interleaved datasets are retained.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the introduction into numbered contributions and combines data curation and composition into Section 3. Detailed task descriptions move into Appendix A and are replaced by rewritten category summaries; prompt templates move from Appendix B to F. The abstract, author list, and acknowledgments also receive edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the scaffolding plot in Figure 4, Table 8, a chess illustration in Figure 7, and five Bagel example panels in Appendix B. Table 1 changes its columns to emphasize CoT modality and training suitability, and numerous illustrations and tables move. The original Bagel Figure 4 is retained as Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The new frontier-model study provides useful evidence about dataset difficulty and the usefulness of supplied traces, while Appendix D adds an important qualification to Bagel's apparent success. Organization and evaluation disclosures also improve. The gains are limited by the absence of a text-only scaffolding control, unquantified Bagel regressions, and removal of the original 142-example test denominator.
